relationships.subject: Fasudil
relationships.evidence_quote: When administered intraperitoneally at the highest tested dose of 30 mg/kg, fasudil significantly reduced mechanical allodynia in the models of SNL-induced neuropathic pain, CCI-induced neuropathic pain, CPSP, capsaicin-induced secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, and sodium iodoacetate-induced osteoarthritic pain [31, 41].

relationships.subject: C3 exoenzyme
relationships.evidence_quote: Extensive studies have shown that intrathecal injections of the C3 exoenzyme (a RhoA inhibitor) or Y27632 significantly diminished pain behaviors in rodent models of neuropathic pain induced by SNL, CCI, TCI, and STZ treatment [16, 17, 29, 30, 34]

relationships.subject: simvastatin
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings suggest that the inhibition of RhoA/ROCK signaling by simvastatin reduced the sensitization of spinal nociceptive transmission.

relationships.subject: LPA receptor 1
relationships.evidence_quote: Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a lipid metabolite released in response to tissue injury, stimulates peripheral nociceptive terminals through the LPA receptor 1 (LPAR1) and its downstream RhoA-ROCK pathway, which has been implicated in the onset of nerve injury-induced neuropathic pain [36].

relationships.subject: RhoA/ROCK signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: The upregulation of Cavα2δ-1 in DRG, triggered by LPA (1 nmol, i.t.) and partial SNL, was eliminated following intrathecal pretreatment with C3 exoenzyme and Y-27632.

key_findings: RhoA/ROCK signaling is dysregulated in DRG and spinal cord across pain models, and its pharmacological inhibition (Y27632, C3, fasudil, simvastatin) alleviates hyperalgesia and allodynia.
Limitations include inhibitor nonspecificity, isoform roles, side effects, and lack of clinical trials in pain.
